entry.title: Apple accidentally reveals (RED) HomePod mini early, and it’s gorgeous
entry.content:
Macworld

It’s Black Friday weekend, and that means a lot of people are shopping for Apple deals. Over at your local Apple Store, you can get gift cards up to $300 when you buy a new MacBook, $100 on an iPhone or Apple Watch, or $25 if you buy a HomePod mini 2. And if you’re really lucky, you’ll get to walk out with a special-edition model no one else has.

It was reported last week that Apple plans to launch two new Product RED devices this week: HomePod mini and AirPods Max. We’re expecting the new products to arrive sometime this week, but apparently Apple Stores have gotten stock already, because a few have accidentally put them on shelves already, much to the surprise of shoppers.

How could this happen? Since the (RED) HomePod mini isn’t technically a new product, Apple likely shipped them to stores early so they can go on shelves as soon as they’re announced. And if employees are rushing and scrambling to keep shelves stocked throughout a busy weekend, it’s very easy to grab one of the boxes that aren’t supposed to be out yet.

Photos of the Product RED HomePod mini have been circulating on social media, and they’re gorgeous. Compared to the relatively staid colors of the HomePod mini 2 (white, pink, blue, green, midnight), the Product RED option is bright and bold, with a festive flair that will look great with your holiday decorations.

We haven’t seen photos of the Product RED AirPods Max yet, which are expected to be mostly silver with red accents. Both Product RED models should arrive early next week, probably on Tuesday.

entry.title: Best time to buy AirPods in 2026: Buy now or wait?
entry.content:
Macworld

In this guide we’ll explain when the best time is to buy each AirPods model, whether you should buy now or wait, which older AirPods are worth considering at clearance prices, and the times of year when you’re most likely to find a bargain.

Black Friday weekend is the best time to buy AirPods. If you want AirPods Pro 3, we’ve seen them drop to $149 in the U.S. and £155.98 in the U.K., the lowest prices we’ve tracked. AirPods Max 2 are also on sale in both countries, while the best discounts on AirPods 5 so far are in the U.K.

Apple introduced AirPods 5 in September 2026 and announced AirPods Max 2 in March 2026. AirPods Pro 3 arrived in September 2025. If you’re happy with the features of the current models, we’d focus on getting a good price on one of Apple’s current range of AirPods during the Black Friday weekend.

Best Black Friday AirPods deals: U.S.

  • AirPods Pro 3: $149 ($100 off at Amazon, MSRP $249)
  • AirPods Max 2: $419 ($130 off at Amazon, MSRP $549)

Best Black Friday AirPods deals: U.K.

  • AirPods Pro 3: £155.98 (£63 off at Amazon, RRP £219).
  • AirPods 5 (wireless charging case): £119 (£20 off at Amazon, RRP £139).
  • AirPods Max 2: £449 (£50 off at Amazon, MSRP £499)

PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 28, 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this throughout the Black Friday weekend

When to buy AirPods: At a glance

What is the worst time to buy AirPods?

The worst time to buy AirPods is generally immediately before a major sale, or just before Apple replaces the model you’re considering.

If Black Friday or Prime Day is a few weeks away and you can manage with your current headphones, wait for the sale before paying full price.

What is the best time to buy AirPods?

Major sales events are generally the best time to buy AirPods. Amazon Prime Day and Black Friday are particularly worth watching because Apple’s headphones and earbuds frequently receive significant retailer discounts.

The savings can be substantial. We’ve seen AirPods Pro 3 fall from $249 to $149 and AirPods Max 2 drop from $549 to $399.

That doesn’t mean you should never buy between sales. If the AirPods you want are already close to their historical low, there’s little reason to wait simply because another sales event will eventually arrive.

Should you buy AirPods now or wait?

  • Buy now if your model is near its lowest price

Foundry

If the AirPods you want are already near their lowest tracked price, we’d buy during Black Friday weekend. A better deal could appear on Cyber Monday, but the current offer could sell out first.

Read our AirPods Buying Guide to understand how the different AirPods compare and find out which is best for you.

Should you buy AirPods 5 now or wait?

Buy, especially if you are in the U.K. where at £119, the Wireless Charging Case version is only £10 more than the standard model.

We recommend: Apple AirPods 5

Price When Reviewed: $129
Best Prices Today: $129 at Amazon | $129 at Apple United States | $129 at B&H

The AirPods 5 only arrived in September 2026, so there’s little reason to wait for another generation. They are also much easier to recommend than the AirPods 4 they replace because Active Noise Cancellation is now standard.

AirPods 5 start at $129 with a USB-C charging case. Apple also sells a $149 version with a Wireless Charging Case, which adds wireless charging, a speaker for Find My, volume adjustment by swiping the stems and slightly longer battery life.

The new generation also brings improved sound and stronger noise cancellation. Apple says AirPods 5 remove up to 50 percent more external noise than AirPods 4 with ANC.

We think the $149 Wireless Charging Case version is the better choice for most buyers because it costs only $20 more and adds several useful features.

Our recommendation: Buy AirPods 5 if you prefer an open-ear design. AirPods 5 haven’t received a significant Prime Day discount, so there’s little reason to rush unless you want them now. Buy AirPods 5 if you prefer an open fit.

Should you buy AirPods Pro 3 now or wait?

  • Buy – At $149 in the U.S., AirPods Pro 3 cost the same as AirPods 5 with the Wireless Charging Case.

We recommend: Apple AirPods Pro 3

Price When Reviewed: $249
Best Prices Today: $149 at Amazon | $149 at Walmart | $199.99 at B&H

AirPods Pro 3 launched in September 2025 and remain Apple’s most capable earbuds. They improve on AirPods Pro 2 with a more comfortable and secure fit, stronger noise cancellation, improved battery life and a heart-rate sensor.

They also have a significant battery-life advantage over AirPods 5, lasting up to eight hours with ANC enabled compared with four or five hours for the two AirPods 5 packages. AirPods Pro 3 additionally support Apple’s Hearing Test, Hearing Aid and Hearing Protection features.

Their $249 price is much higher than the $129/$149 AirPods 5, but discounts can dramatically narrow that gap. AirPods Pro 3 have previously fallen as low as $169, making sales events particularly attractive times to buy.

Our recommendation: Buy if you want the strongest noise isolation, longer battery life, a secure in-ear fit or Apple’s health and hearing features. At full price, compare carefully with AirPods 5; at a substantial discount, AirPods Pro 3 become much more compelling.

Should you buy AirPods Max 2 now or wait?

  • Buy – $419 is a good price and just $20 above the lowest we’ve tracked. In the U.K., £449 matches the lowest price we’ve seen.

We recommend: Apple AirPods Max 2

Price When Reviewed: $549
Best Prices Today: $419 at Amazon | $419 at Walmart | $495 at Best Buy US

AirPods Max 2 are relatively new, so waiting for an imminent replacement isn’t the main concern. The bigger issue is value.

The second-generation model adds the H2 chip and features including Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Voice Isolation and Live Translation. Sound quality, Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency mode remain excellent.

However, our review found that Apple failed to address several longstanding complaints, including the headphones’ weight, Smart Case and inability to be switched off manually.

Our recommendation: Don’t wait for a new generation – Apple isn’t expected to update AirPods Max again soon. Instead, wait for a good discount unless you need them immediately.

Should you buy older or refurbished AirPods?

Foundry

Older AirPods can make sense when retailers are clearing stock, but compare the price with the model that replaced them rather than focusing on the percentage discount from the original MSRP.

You should also be careful when buying an older generation simply because it appears heavily discounted. The percentage saving can be misleading if the replacement model offers significantly more for a similar price. AirPods 5, for example, start at the same $129 price originally charged for AirPods 4 without ANC, but now include Active Noise Cancellation as standard.

You should be particularly cautious when buying AirPods from marketplaces or unfamiliar sellers. Counterfeit AirPods can closely resemble genuine products, and unusually low prices – particularly on second-hand marketplaces – can be a warning sign.

If you’re considering an older model, check the exact generation, charging case and condition, and make sure the seller is reputable.

When does Apple release new AirPods?

Unlike the iPhone, AirPods don’t follow a simple annual update schedule.

AirPods Pro 3 launched in September 2025, AirPods Max 2 followed in 2026, and Apple introduced AirPods 5 in September 2026.

Because the three main AirPods families have all been updated relatively recently, the current lineup doesn’t present the obvious “wait because a replacement is imminent” problem that sometimes occurs with Apple products.

entry.title: Buying an iPad for your kid? Here’s the one we’d pick
entry.content:
Macworld

Our kids love their iPads. They learn to tap and swipe in seconds, and there’s plenty for them to do as they get older, from playing educational games and drawing with an Apple Pencil to doing homework and watching movies on long car journeys. The harder part is choosing which iPad to buy.

The standard iPad (A16) is the one we’d buy for most kids. It starts at $449/£429 with 128GB of storage, and its 11-inch screen gives them plenty of room for games, schoolwork, and drawing.

The 8.5-inch iPad mini (A20 Pro) is our compact pick. It’s easier for small hands to hold and takes up less room in a bag, but it starts at $699/£699. For $50/£50 more, the 11-inch iPad Air (M4) gives older kids more screen space for drawing, editing video, and working on school projects. It also supports Apple’s Magic Keyboard for longer writing assignments.

Alongside our top picks, we explain whether you should buy an iPad for your child, whether it’s worth paying extra for cellular, how much storage to get, and how to set limits with parental controls.

How to choose the best iPad for children

Start with what your child will use the iPad for. A smaller iPad is easier for little hands to hold while reading or playing games, especially on trips. A larger screen gives kids more room to draw, edit video, or type up school assignments.

128GB of storage is enough for most kids. Consider 256GB if your child plays several large games, downloads lots of movies for trips, or regularly records and edits video. Downloaded games and movies still take up space on the iPad, even if you pay for iCloud storage.

The standard iPad has plenty of power for everyday games, school apps, and videos. Apple Intelligence, which is missing from the standard iPad, is available on the iPad mini and iPad Air and may be useful for older kids who use their iPad for schoolwork or creative projects. Writing Tools can help them spot spelling and grammar mistakes in their own drafts or turn a long set of notes into a list of key points. In Photos, Clean Up can remove a distracting object from a picture they want to use in a presentation. Parents can restrict features such as Writing Tools and AI image creation through Apple’s parental controls. For help setting up parental controls, see “Should you get an iPad for your child?” below.

If it’s your child’s first iPad, set aside some of your budget for a sturdy case.

Best iPad for kids of all ages

For most children, the standard iPad has enough power and screen space for everyday apps, games, and homework. Choose the iPad mini if your child will often use it one-handed for reading or carry it on trips, where the smaller size makes a real difference.

The 11-inch iPad Air is worth considering for older kids who regularly draw, edit video, or type up school assignments. There’s also a 13-inch Air if they’d benefit from more room to work. For most school and creative projects, the Air has plenty of power without the expense of an iPad Pro.

Why the iPad Air is a good choice: The 11-inch iPad Air (M4) is the upgrade we’d recommend for a tween or teen who regularly uses an iPad for schoolwork and creative projects. It gives them more room than the iPad mini to mark up a PDF, draw, or keep a textbook and their notes open side by side. And at 1.02 pounds (464g) for the Wi-Fi model, it’s still light enough to carry in a school bag.

The fully laminated display brings the image closer to the Pencil tip, so writing and drawing feel more natural than on the standard iPad. Both Air sizes support the Apple Pencil (USB-C) and Apple Pencil Pro. The optional Magic Keyboard makes longer assignments easier to type, but factor its cost into your budget and check that the iPad can run the apps your child’s school requires. See which Apple Pencil works with your iPad. 

The M4 chip has plenty of power for demanding games, video editing, and working in several apps, and it supports Apple Intelligence. Budding filmmakers can shoot 4K video at up to 60fps with the 12MP rear camera and edit it on the same device. Apple rates both sizes for up to 10 hours of video playback or web browsing over Wi-Fi, though sustained gaming and video editing can drain the battery faster. The base 128GB should be enough for schoolwork and everyday apps. Consider 256GB if your child downloads lots of games or movies or regularly edits video. Apple also offers 512GB and 1TB models. 

The 11-inch Air starts at $749/£749, just $50/£50 more than the iPad mini (A20 Pro). It’s the size we’d choose for school. The 13-inch Air starts at $949/£949 and makes more sense if your child mainly works at a desk and will regularly use the extra space for drawing or working with two apps. Both come in Blue, Purple, Starlight, and Space Gray. For everyday games, videos, and occasional homework, we’d still buy the cheaper standard iPad (A16)

Should you get an iPad for your child?

An iPad can be a good buy if it suits your child’s age, maturity, and interests, and you’re comfortable setting limits and supervising how they use it. It’s easy to pick up, especially if they’ve already used your iPhone, and what they can do with it changes as they get older.

  • Toddlers and preschoolers: For children under two, prioritize play and interaction. With preschoolers, start with short activities you can do together, such as drawing or playing a learning game. And if an episode of Bluey buys you enough time to get dinner on the table, fair enough. Apple’s Guided Access can keep a younger child in one app while they use it.
  • Elementary/Primary school kids: An iPad can help with homework and give kids room to explore their interests. They can try coding with a tool like Scratch, practice a language, or use a compatible Apple Pencil to draw and paint.
  • Tweens and teens: An iPad can be useful for research, school projects, and creative work – many schools require students to have a device on which to do their homework. A budding filmmaker can shoot and edit a video on the same device, while a child who loves to draw can use it as a digital sketchbook.

What are the child safety and screen time options?

Before you hand over the iPad, check the age ratings and privacy settings for the apps your child wants to use. A game may look fine until you find out it has public chat or lets strangers send friend requests. Review those settings together, restrict contact with people they don’t know, and show them how to block and report someone. Make sure they know they can come to you if anything upsets them.

Apple’s parental controls let you manage how much time your child spends in apps, what content they can access, and who they can communicate with in supported apps. Communication Safety can blur detected nudity in shared photos and videos in supported apps. In iPadOS 27, it can also blur detected gore and violent content.

The settings you start with will depend on your child’s age and maturity. For ages 3–7, you might turn off Safari and choose a handful of apps they can use. For ages 8–12, start with communication limits and review the safety settings in their favorite games. For ages 13–17, agree on a daily limit for social apps and schedule Downtime around bedtime.

If you want a starting point for screen time, the American Academy of Pediatrics says families might set limits of less than an hour a day for toddlers and preschoolers and around one to two hours of recreational screen time for school-age children and teens. An hour learning French, finishing homework, or watching gaming videos can serve very different purposes. Pay attention to what your child is doing on the iPad and whether it’s pushing bedtime later or crowding out sleep, exercise, or time with friends.

How to set up parental controls on a child’s iPad

Apple redesigned its parental controls in iPadOS 27. You can now choose which types of apps are available at different points in the day, such as during school or after homework, and set a shared daily time budget for games, entertainment, and social media. There’s also a new Ask to Browse feature that lets your child request access to a website and lets you approve it from your own device.

Here’s how to set up Parental Controls:

  1. You need to give your child their own Apple Account before you can set up Parental Controls for them. On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Family > Add Member. Choose Create Child Account or invite your child if they already have an account. To use the redesigned controls, you will need to update the devices listed under Settings > Family > View Family Devices to version 27 or later of their Apple software. Then go to Settings > Family > Get Started and follow the prompts.
  2. Set daily limits and a schedule. On your own iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Family > [your child’s name] > Time Allowances. Set a daily time budget or adjust the time allowed for categories such as Games and Social Media. To set hours for school nights or weekends, return to your child’s settings, open Screen Time Schedule, turn on Schedule, then tap Add Schedule and choose the days and hours.
  3. Choose what your child can access and who they can contact. Start at Settings > Family > [your child’s name] on your own iPhone or iPad. From there, you can set the following:
    • App downloads and purchases: Under Apps & Websites, open Restrictions > Ask to Buy and turn on Require Purchase Approval. To block app installs or in-app purchases outright, use the App Store settings under Apps & Websites.
    • Web browsing: Go to Apps & Websites > Restrictions, then tap Filtering under Websites. Choose Limit Adult Websites to filter adult content or Approved Websites Only to have your child ask before visiting a new site in Safari or another supported browser.
    • Age ratings: Open Content & Privacy Restrictions. Under Content Restrictions, pick a category such as apps, movies, or TV shows, then choose the rating you want to allow.
    • Messages and calls: Go to Allowed Contacts > During Screen Time > Contacts Only to limit who your child can communicate with in Messages, FaceTime, and Phone. To approve new contacts yourself, turn on Manage Contacts and leave Allow Contact Editing off.
  4. You can use Guided Access to temporarily lock an iPad to one app, which is handy when a young child is drawing or playing a game. On your child’s iPad, go to Settings > Accessibility > Guided Access and turn it on. Open the app you want your child to use, then triple-click the top button or the Home button if the iPad has one. Select Guided Access if prompted, then tap Start.

We have more guidance in How to set up an iPad or iPhone for kids.

Recommended iPad accessories for kids

  • Protective Gear: For younger users, a durable case and screen protector are essential to prevent damage from drops. iPads are hardy but not indestructible. It is highly recommended to invest in a durable, kid-proof case and a screen protector to mitigate the risk of cracked glass.
  • Creative Tools: An Apple Pencil (1st gen, USB-C, or Pro depending on the model) can transform the tablet into a digital art studio. See: Which Apple Pencil to find out which one to buy. We also have a roundup of the best iPad styluses, if you want something cheaper.
  • Learning Kits: Systems like Osmo use physical blocks and “Reflective AI technology” to teach coding and STEM skills to children aged 5-12.
  • Audio: Wireless headphones, such as Beats Flex, are recommended for travel to keep children entertained without tangled wires.

FAQ

1.

Can I set screen time limits and use parental controls?

Yes. With Family Sharing, you can manage Screen Time from your own iPhone or iPad. You can set limits for individual apps, schedule when your child can use them, and restrict access to websites and age-rated content. See How to set up parental controls on a child’s iPad above for the steps.

2.

Do kids need a cellular iPad?

We’d buy the Wi-Fi model for most kids. For an occasional trip, download shows and games that work offline before you leave, or share your iPhone’s connection using Personal Hotspot if your phone plan supports it.

Wi-Fi + Cellular is worth considering if your child regularly needs internet access away from Wi-Fi and you won’t be there to share your connection. The cellular model costs more up front, and you’ll need a compatible cellular data plan to use that connection.

3.

Is 128GB enough for a child’s iPad?

Yes. We’d choose 128GB for most kids, especially if they mainly stream video, use school apps, and play a few games. Pay for 256GB if your child keeps several large games installed, downloads lots of shows for trips, or records and edits video regularly.

iCloud can help with photos and files, but installed games and videos downloaded for offline viewing still use space on the iPad. If you’re buying refurbished, we’d aim for at least 128GB. See iCloud prices.

Is there education pricing for iPads?

If those prices seem steep, Apple offers education pricing in the U.S. and U.K. to eligible college and university students, including those who’ve been accepted, and to parents buying on their behalf. Having a child in elementary or high school doesn’t qualify you on its own. If you’re shopping for college or university, see our guides to getting an Apple student discount and the best iPads for students. If you’re buying your child their first tablet, check our roundup of the best iPad deals before paying full price.

If you have older children, then take a look at our guide to the best iPads for students.

Should I buy a refurbished iPad?

If you’re shopping secondhand, check the generation before you buy. The 8th-generation iPad, 5th-generation iPad mini, 3rd-generation iPad Air, and earlier models in those lines can’t run iPadOS 27. The 9th-generation iPad still supports it, but we’d pay a little more for a 10th-generation model.

A refurbished or hand-me-down 10th-generation iPad is a good first tablet for games, videos, and homework. The 64GB version is fine for light use, but that storage can fill up quickly if your child downloads lots of games or movies. If you’re paying extra for the 256GB version, compare its price with a new iPad (A16), which starts at 128GB.

If you want something smaller, look for a refurbished iPad mini. For more room to draw or do schoolwork, consider an 11-inch iPad Air. Compare the refurbished price with the best deal you can find on a new model with the same amount of storage. If the saving is small, we’d buy the newer iPad.

You can sometimes find recent models for around 15% off in Apple’s Certified Refurbished store. Apple’s refurbished iPads come with a new battery, a new outer shell, and the same one-year limited warranty as a new iPad. We’ve bought several refurbished models from Apple over the years, and they’ve all been as good as new.

If a third-party seller offers a better price, check what it guarantees about battery condition, how long the warranty lasts, and whether you can return the iPad. See our guide to where to buy a refurbished iPad.

PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 28, 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout the Black Friday weekend

Black Friday is a great time to buy an Apple Watch, with retailers discounting everything from the affordable SE to the premium Ultra. Apple Watch deals this Black Friday are already beating some of October Prime Day’s best prices. Amazon has listed the 42mm Apple Watch Series 12 for $299 in the U.S. and £319.98 in the U.K., saving $100 and £49, respectively. In the U.S., the 40mm Apple Watch SE 3 is our budget pick at $179 and the Ultra 4 was $129 off at Amazon, but that’s dropped to $25 off now.

The standout U.K. deal is the Apple Watch Ultra 3 at £495. That’s £224 less than the discounted Ultra 4 at £719. The Ultra 4 offers longer battery life and newer health sensors, but if you mainly want the rugged design, diving features, and satellite connectivity, the Ultra 3 is the better buy at those prices. 

Below, we compare the latest prices with previous lows and explain when an older model is worth choosing. For example, the 42mm Series 11 at £260 saves almost £100 compared with the equivalent Series 12 deal above. That’s worth considering if you don’t need the newer health features. For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our Apple Black Friday deals roundups of the best Mac deals, iPad deals and AirPods deals.

Between November 27 and November 30, Apple will include a $50 U.S. or £40 U.K. Apple Gift Card with an eligible Apple Watch Series 12 or SE 3 bought directly from Apple. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 comes with a $100 U.S. or £80 U.K. gift card. See our guide to Apple’s Black Friday shopping event for the full offer.

Which Apple Watch should you buy this Black Friday?

Apple Watch Series 12 – Our best overall choice

Apple

The Series 12 is the Apple Watch we recommend for most people. It combines Apple’s new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate measurements, a Readiness score, and a tougher display with up to 24 hours of battery life.

A worthwhile Black Friday discount could make it an attractive purchase, but compare it with remaining Series 11 stock. The older model has the same quoted battery life, so a substantial saving may outweigh the newer health features.

U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has discounted the 42mm GPS Series 12 to $299, $100 off and the lowest price we’ve seen for the 42mm model. The 46mm version is also $100 off.

U.K. Black Friday price: Amazon has the 42mm Apple Watch Series 12 for £329 (£40 off) and the 46mm model for £359 (£60 off). At those prices, the larger screen costs just £30 more.

Apple’s deal: Apple will give $50 U.S. or £40 U.K. Apple Gift Card with an eligible Apple Watch Series 12. Amazon’s Series 12 discount in the U.S. is worth more than Apple’s $50 gift card.

Apple Watch Ultra 4 – Best for battery life and outdoor adventures

Apple

The Ultra 4 is our choice for endurance athletes, outdoor enthusiasts, and buyers who prioritize battery life. It offers up to 50 hours of normal use, satellite communication, precision dual-frequency GPS, diving features, and Apple’s new Health Sensing System.

It’s more watch than most people need. Compare it with the Ultra 3, though, which retains many of its outdoor features but has a shorter 42-hour battery-life rating.

U.S. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought the Ultra 4 down to $774, a $25 saving. On Black Friday itselfm Amazon was selling the Apple Watch Ultra 4 for $649.99 on Amazon: that’s $149 off, however that deal has sold out and the price has returned to the Prime Day low of $774 now.

U.K. Black Friday price: The Ultra 4 remained at its full £749 price during October Prime Day, but we’ve already seen it drop by £30 to £719 at Amazon.

Apple’s deal: The Apple Watch Ultra 4 comes with a $100 U.S. or £80 U.K. Apple gift card if you buy direct from Apple.

Apple Watch SE 3 – Our best budget choice

Apple / Amazon

The SE 3 is the best-value option for buyers who want the core Apple Watch experience. It includes an always-on display, temperature sensing, fast charging, and the S10 chip, but lacks ECG, blood oxygen monitoring, and the newer Health Sensing System.

It remains part of Apple’s current lineup despite launching in 2025. A strong Black Friday offer could make it an excellent affordable purchase, although its previous discounts mean there’s little reason to settle for a token reduction.

U.S. Black Friday price: Both last Black Friday and October Prime Day brought the 40mm GPS model to $199 and the 44mm version to $229 – $50 below their regular prices. This Black Friday, the U.S. price is down to $179, $70 off at Amazon.

U.K. Black Friday price: Black Friday 2025 and October Prime Day brought the 40mm GPS model to £199 and the 44mm version to £229, saving £20. So far the Apple Watch SE 3, 40mm has dropped to £199 (£20 off at Amazon) and the 44mm model is £223, £26 off.

Apple’s deal: Apple will give $50 U.S. or £40 U.K. Apple Gift Card with an eligible Apple Watch SE 3 when purchased from Apple.

Apple Watch Ultra 3 – Best clearance option for outdoor enthusiasts

Apple

The Ultra 3 is worth considering if you want a rugged Apple Watch without paying for the latest model. It offers satellite communication, dual-frequency GPS, diving features, and up to 42 hours of battery life.

You give up the Ultra 4’s longer battery life and newer Health Sensing System. Compare their actual selling prices: the Ultra 3 needs to be sufficiently cheaper to justify choosing the older generation.

U.S. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the Ultra 3 fell to $699, $100 saving. Our October Prime Day coverage found only used models, so it didn’t identify a comparable new-stock offer. So far this November we’ve seen the Apple Watch Ultra 3 for $649, but it’s now out of stock and you can get the Ultra 4 for that price.

U.K. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the Ultra 3 was £719, or £30 off. October Prime Day listed it at £569. The price is even lower this November – you can get it for £495 at Argos, which is £254 less than the usual Apple Watch Ultra 4 price. (Alternative link for Argos)

Apple Watch Series 11 – Best clearance option for everyday use

Apple Watch Series 11

The Series 11 could be a better-value everyday watch than the Series 12 if the price gap is large enough. It has the same quoted 24-hour battery life, although it lacks the newer Health Sensing System and Audio Intelligence features.

For buyers who don’t need those additions, a substantial clearance discount could be more useful than a small saving on the latest model.

U.S. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the 42mm GPS Series 11 reached $339, while the 46mm version was $359 – savings of $60 and $70, respectively. We are only seeing used models in the U.S. at the moment.

U.K. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought the 42mm Series 11 to £259 and the 46mm version to £299. Earlier in November the Apple Watch Series 11 46mm model was £260, £159 less than the equivalent Series 12, but that has now sold out.

Latest Apple Watch deals

Compare current prices for each configuration with its full price and our lowest recorded price. We’ve highlighted prices matching our recorded lows in bold.

U.S. deals

U.K. deals

Should you buy an Apple Watch now?

Black Friday is here, and we’d buy now if the Apple Watch you want is at or near its lowest price for the same size and configuration. Several U.S. deals are already better than the prices we saw during October Prime Day, and there are savings in the U.K. too. If you have a particular size, color, or band in mind, it’s worth buying while it’s in stock.

U.S. Amazon has the Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS) for $299 in 42mm and $349 in 46mm, both $50 less than during October Prime Day. The Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS) is $179 in 40mm and $209 in 44mm, both $20 below their October prices. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is $699, down $75 from its October Prime Day price of $774.

U.K. Amazon’s £199 deal on the 40mm Apple Watch SE 3 (GPS) matches its October Prime Day price. The 44mm model is £223, down £6 from £229 in October. At these prices, the larger screen costs £24 more.

Check other retailers before you order, especially if Amazon sells out of your preferred configuration. Last Black Friday, Walmart offered $150 off the Series 10, while U.K. shoppers could save up to £130 at Currys or get the Ultra 2 for £200 below its original price at Argos. Our guide to the best time to buy an Apple Watch has more advice on choosing when to purchase.

Should you buy an older Apple Watch?

David Price / Foundry

Don’t assume an older Apple Watch is a bad buy. The Series 11 and Ultra 3 are only one generation old and can make excellent purchases if they’re substantially cheaper than the Series 12 or Ultra 4. Both retain many of their replacements’ core features, although you miss the newer Health Sensing System and, with the Ultra 3, the Ultra 4’s longer battery life.

Compare actual selling prices, matching case size, material, connectivity, and band where possible. A $50 difference between a Series 11 and Series 12 may not be enough to justify giving up the newer model’s health features, whereas a substantially larger saving could change the calculation. A discounted Series 11 could also be worth considering alongside the SE 3 if a small premium gets you features you’ll use.

Be much more cautious with the Series 8, SE 2, and original Ultra: those models cannot run watchOS 27. The Series 9 is the oldest standard Apple Watch compatible with the latest software, while the Ultra 2 is the oldest supported Ultra and the SE 3 is the only supported SE. Missing the latest software doesn’t make an older watch unusable, but it makes it harder to recommend as a purchase today.

The Series 9, Series 10, and Ultra 2 can still be worth considering at sufficiently low prices. However, compatibility with today’s software doesn’t guarantee how many future upgrades they’ll receive. Weigh the savings against the watch’s age and features, rather than assuming every supported generation offers equally good value.

Apple Watch deals to avoid

David Price / Foundry

Don’t let a bigger advertised discount tempt you into paying more for a cellular Apple Watch you won’t use. If your iPhone is usually nearby, a GPS model can already handle calls, messages, and notifications through your phone. It can also track runs, use Apple Pay, and play downloaded music without your iPhone. As our experience testing a cellular Apple Watch showed, the extra connectivity may add little to everyday use.

Cellular is worth considering if you regularly leave your iPhone behind and want to remain contactable without Wi-Fi, or you’re setting up a watch for a child without an iPhone. Otherwise, you could pay extra for the hardware and then add an ongoing mobile-plan charge for a feature you rarely need. You don’t have to activate a plan on a cellular model, so it can still be a good buy if its sale price matches or beats the GPS version. Our GPS versus cellular Apple Watch guide explains the trade-offs.

Check the rest of the configuration, too. A premium case material or expensive band can make a heavily discounted watch cost more than a simpler version that meets your needs. Judge offers against previous selling prices as well as the advertised reduction: a large saving from the original launch price doesn’t necessarily mean exceptional value. Check any spending requirements, contracts, trade-ins, or rebates attached to offers advertising a “free” Apple Watch.

Finally, check whether you’re buying a new, refurbished, or used watch, who is selling it, and what warranty and returns policy apply. For a used or refurbished model, check the stated battery condition and confirm that it has been removed from the previous owner’s account, with Activation Lock turned off. Make sure the watch is compatible with your iPhone before ordering.

How we choose Apple Watch deals

Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on Apple Watch reviews and everyday wear. We consider comfort, performance, battery life, charging, health and fitness features, and value – not just the specifications or advertised saving.

Our testing helps us explain which features are worth paying for. For example, our Series 12 review assessed battery life and charging performance alongside its newer health features. We also draw on everyday experience: our cellular Apple Watch testing examines whether staying connected without an iPhone justified the extra hardware and subscription costs.

We combine those findings with current prices and previous lows to judge whether an offer represents good value. We check the generation, case size, material, connectivity, and included band so that comparisons reflect what you’re actually buying. Older models can be worthwhile clearance purchases, but only when their prices make sense alongside discounted replacements.

Our Best Apple Watch guide explains why the most expensive model isn’t necessarily the right choice: your budget, wrist size, activities, and the features you need all matter.

For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our roundups of the best Mac deals, iPad deals, and AirPods deals.

Which iPad should you buy this Black Friday?

M4 iPad Air – Our best all-round choice

Apple Inc

The iPad Air offers a strong balance of performance, screen size, and price without the premium cost of the Pro. The 11-inch model suits buyers who prioritize portability, while the 13-inch version gives you more room for multitasking and creative work.

A good Black Friday discount could make either size an attractive purchase. Compare storage capacities carefully, though: a larger advertised saving on a high-capacity model isn’t necessarily better value if you don’t need the extra space.

U.K. Black Friday price: Amazon has £80 to £109 off the iPad Air configurations. For example, you can get the 11-inch M4 iPad Air with 128GB for £669, down from the usual £749. These are reasonable savings, although we saw better discounts during October Prime Day, with up to £144 off. Last Black Friday, selected M3 Air configurations received £100 discounts.

Apple’s deal: You can get a $100/£80 Apple Gift Card when you buy an 11-inch or 13-inch M4 iPad Air from Apple, which is similar to the Amazon U.K. deal.

iPad Pro – Best for demanding creative work

Apple Inc

The iPad Pro is the option for buyers who need Apple’s highest-end tablet performance and premium display. It comes in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes, but its capabilities – and price – will exceed what many people need for browsing, streaming, and everyday apps.

We’d look for a substantial saving rather than buy simply because it’s the most powerful iPad. Compare discounted M4 iPad Pro models, too: an older Pro could offer better value if its price is sufficiently below the equivalent M5 configuration.

The new iPad mini went on sale on November 6, replacing the A17 Pro model. It brings an 8.5-inch OLED display, the A20 Pro chip, and a thinner, lighter design, making it the option to consider if you want a compact iPad with the latest hardware.

Because it has only just arrived, we’d expect initial discounts to be smaller than clearance savings on its predecessor. The older A17 Pro mini could still be worthwhile at a sufficiently low price, but compare the savings with what you give up – particularly the new display.

U.S. Black Friday price: The A20 Pro mini wasn’t available during October Prime Day or last Black Friday. Right now, Amazon has it for $599, $100 off, and the best price we’ve seen so far. Latest iPad Deals

Check below to find the best price we are seeing right now for each configuration, compared to the best price we have ever seen and the full price. Bold prices indicate offers that match the lowest price we’ve recorded for that configuration. All prices are for Wi-Fi models with standard glass unless stated otherwise.

U.K. deals

Should you buy an iPad now?

Foundry

Black Friday is here, and we’d buy now if you find a good deal on the iPad you want. Compare prices for the same generation, screen size, storage, and connectivity. If a deal is at or near the lowest price we’ve seen for that configuration, it’s worth taking while it’s in stock.

If you’re buying an iPad Air and already plan to get an Apple Pencil or keyboard from Apple, consider Apple’s Black Friday gift card. For the iPad Pro, check Amazon first. We’ve seen the 11-inch M5 iPad Pro with 1TB for $299.01 off in the U.S. and £150 off in the U.K. Both discounts exceed the value of Apple’s gift card.

Check what the iPad sold for before Apple raised prices in June. During October Prime Day, the 128GB A16 iPad was $399 and the 11-inch M4 iPad Air with 128GB was $649. Both were on sale and still cost more than they did at full price before June.

We’d buy the M4 iPad Air or M5 iPad Pro at a good price this Black Friday. We expect both models to stick around until 2027. We’d be more cautious about the A16 iPad, which lacks Apple Intelligence. Unless you find a substantial discount, we’d wait for a potentially more capable entry-level model. See our guide to the best time to buy an iPad.

In the U.S., the new 128GB iPad mini (A20 Pro) is $599, down $100 from its $699 list price. That’s the deal we’d pick if you want the latest model. The older 128GB iPad mini (A17 Pro) is $499 if you’d rather save another $100. In the U.K., the new iPad mini still starts at £699, so we’d wait for a discount if you’re in no hurry.

Should you buy an older iPad?

Foundry

An older iPad can be a good buy if its price reflects its age and the features you give up. Compare its actual selling price with the discounted price of its replacement, matching screen size, storage, and connectivity where possible. A large saving from an old launch price doesn’t necessarily make it better value.

The M3 iPad Air and M4 iPad Pro are worth considering at substantial clearance discounts. Both remain capable options, and you may get more benefit from a lower price or additional storage than from the latest processor. However, if the newer equivalent costs only slightly more, the saving may not justify choosing the older generation.

The A17 Pro iPad mini also deserves consideration now that the A20 Pro model has arrived. It supports Apple Intelligence and remains a capable compact tablet, but you miss the newer model’s OLED display, faster processor, and thinner, lighter design. We’d want a meaningful saving rather than a small reduction from its former asking price.

Be more cautious with much older models. Check whether they support the current version of iPadOS and the apps and features you need. Compatibility today doesn’t guarantee how many future software upgrades they’ll receive. Apple Intelligence support also varies: don’t assume every older Air, Pro, or mini includes it.

If you already own an Apple Pencil or keyboard, check compatibility before changing generations. Keeping compatible accessories could make an older iPad better value, while replacing them could erase part of your saving. Our iPad buying guide explains the differences between the ranges.

iPad deals to avoid

Check the exact configuration before comparing offers. Retailer listings can emphasize iPad, Air, or Pro without making the generation obvious. Confirm the chip, screen size, storage capacity, and whether you’re buying Wi-Fi or Wi-Fi + Cellular. A cheaper listing may be a different model rather than a better deal.

Don’t let a large advertised discount tempt you into paying for storage or connectivity you won’t use. A heavily reduced high-capacity or cellular iPad can still cost more than a simpler configuration that meets your needs. Compare the final purchase prices, rather than assuming the biggest saving represents the best value.

Check whether the price includes nano-texture glass, too. This optional finish (on the 1TB and 2TB M5 iPad Pro and the 256GB and 512GB A20 Pro iPad mini) reduces glare and makes fingerprints and oily smudges less noticeable, which can be useful if reflections make your iPad difficult to see in bright rooms or outdoors. It avoids much of the washed-out appearance associated with ordinary matte finishes, but contrast can drop at some viewing angles and the surface may be more scratch-sensitive. Availability depends on the model and storage configuration, so you could end up paying for both the finish and additional storage. If reflections rarely bother you, standard glass may be better value. Read our guide to nano-texture glass and whether you need it.

Our iPad buying guide considers cellular a luxury for most buyers. If you mainly use your iPad somewhere with Wi-Fi, you may get little benefit from the extra hardware. For occasional use elsewhere, sharing your iPhone’s connection through Personal Hotspot can be a more economical option.

Cellular makes more sense if you regularly need an independent connection while commuting or traveling; it also adds built-in GPS for accurate location tracking. Factor in any data-plan charges and compare the total cost of a contract with buying outright. A cellular model can still be worthwhile if its sale price matches or beats the equivalent Wi-Fi version—you don’t have to activate a data plan simply because the hardware is included.

Judge savings against previous selling prices as well as Apple’s current price. Following June’s price increases, a discounted iPad may still cost more than it did earlier in the year. Also distinguish a cash discount from a gift-card offer: a gift card doesn’t reduce the amount you pay for the iPad and is useful only if you’ll spend it.

Check what any bundle includes. A keyboard, case, or stylus doesn’t automatically make an offer better value, particularly if the accessories aren’t the versions you want. Read the conditions attached to “free” iPads, trade-in promotions, contracts, and rebates before comparing their total cost with buying outright.

Finally, check whether the iPad is new, refurbished, or used, who is selling it, and what warranty and returns policy apply. For used or refurbished models, look for information about battery condition and confirm that Activation Lock has been removed. Be cautious about devices that remain tied to a previous owner or an organization’s management system.

How we choose iPad deals

Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on iPad reviews and everyday use. We consider performance, display quality, portability, battery life, and accessory support alongside price to explain which iPads suit different buyers.

Our reviews help us assess whether paying more brings practical benefits. A faster processor or premium display may matter for demanding creative work, while a less expensive iPad can be perfectly capable of browsing, streaming, and schoolwork. We also consider the cost of keyboards, Apple Pencils, and other accessories when judging an iPad’s value.

We combine those findings with current prices and previous offers, matching the generation, screen size, storage, and connectivity so that comparisons reflect what you’re actually buying. Following Apple’s June price increases, we also consider earlier selling prices rather than relying solely on savings against today’s recommended price.

Older models can be worthwhile clearance purchases, but only when their prices make sense alongside newer alternatives. Our iPad buying guide explains the differences between the ranges, while our purchase-timing guide helps you decide whether to buy now or wait.

  • AirPods Pro 3: £155.98 (£63 off at Amazon, RRP £219).
  • AirPods 5 (wireless charging case): £119 (£20 off at Amazon, RRP £139).
  • AirPods Max 2: £449 (£50 off at Amazon, MSRP £499)

PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 28, 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout the Black Friday weekend

Black Friday is a great time to buy AirPods, with retailers competing to offer discounts across Apple’s earbuds and over-ear headphones. Previous sales have brought substantial savings on established models, clearance bargains on older generations, and even discounts on newly released AirPods. But the biggest percentage saving doesn’t necessarily mean the best buy: an older pair needs to be sufficiently cheaper than its replacement to justify missing out on newer features.

The best Black Friday AirPods deal we’ve seen so far is on the AirPods Pro 3. Amazon has listed them for $149 in the U.S. and £156 in the U.K., saving $100 and £63, respectively. If Amazon lists the AirPods Pro as out of stock, the $149 deal is also available at Walmart. That’s a much bigger U.S. discount than the roughly $30 off we saw last Black Friday. If you prefer over-ear headphones, Amazon has also listed the AirPods Max 2 for $419 in the U.S., $130 off and just $20 above the lowest price we’ve tracked.

If you prefer an open-ear fit, AirPods 5 are the cheaper option: in the U.K. we’ve seen £20 off the wireless charging AirPods 5, at £119, while it was still at its regular $149 U.S. price at our last check. Below, we explain which AirPods to choose and how the offers compare with previous discounts. For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our Apple Black Friday deals roundups of the best Mac deals, iPad deals, and Apple Watch deals.

Apple’s own Black Friday offer started November 27 and runs until November 30, 2026. You can buy eligible AirPods directly from Apple, and receive a gift card to use on a future purchase. More details here: Apple Black Friday 2026: Up to $300/£240 in gift cards – full list of eligible products.

Which AirPods should you buy this Black Friday?

AirPods Pro 3 – Our best overall choice

Apple

AirPods Pro 3 are especially worth considering if you want strong noise cancellation, a secure in-ear fit, or Apple’s hearing-health features. Their foam-infused ear tips help improve the fit, while an in-ear heart-rate sensor adds another reason to choose them over standard AirPods. Battery life is rated at up to eight hours with noise cancellation enabled.

For most buyers looking for noise-isolating earbuds, these would be our first choice. Older AirPods Pro 2 are worth considering only when the clearance savings are substantial.

U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has slashed $100 off the AirPods Pro 3, to just $149, the same price as the AirPods 5 with wireless charging case and below their previous all-time low of $169. Amazon sold out for a day or so, but got more stock; if that happens again, Walmart also has them at that price.

U.K. Black Friday price: Earlier in November, AirPods Pro 3 were £30 off in the U.K., before rising to £200, then dropping down to £174, only to return to £200. Amazon now has the AirPods Pro 3 for £155.98, £63.02 off the £219 RRP! We recommend being quick because that price is going up and down like a Swanee whistle.

Apple’s deal: You can get a $50/£40 gift card with your purchase.

AirPods 5 – Best for buyers who prefer earbuds without silicone tips

Apple

AirPods 5 offer a lower-cost entry point and an open-ear design for people who don’t like silicone-tipped earbuds. They include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, alongside Transparency mode and Adaptive Audio.

Check which charging case you’re buying. The Wireless Charging Case package adds wireless charging, longer battery life, a Find My speaker, and volume adjustment by swiping the stems. It’s our preferred package when the price difference is small.

U.S. Black Friday price: We’ve not seen a discount yet on the AirPods 5.

U.K. Black Friday price: You can get £20 off the AirPods 5 with wireless charging in the U.K. That’s the same as Apple’s gift card ‘saving’.

Apple’s deal: Get a $25/£20 gift card with the purchase of AirPods 5.

AirPods Max 2 – Best for over-ear listening

Apple

AirPods Max 2 are the option to consider if you specifically want over-ear headphones. The March 2026 update introduced Apple’s H2 chip and improved noise cancellation, while retaining the premium design and a choice of colors.

We find them difficult to recommend at full price, so the size of the discount matters. Compare any offer with previous sale prices rather than judging it solely against Apple’s asking price.

U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has the AirPods Max 2 for $419, a $130 saving.

U.K. Black Friday price: AirPods Max 2 are reduced to £449 at Amazon, £50 off. If you’d prefer the money off up-front, buy from Apple to get a £60 gift card with AirPods Max purchases.

Apple’s deal: Get a $75/£60 gift card with the purchase of AirPods Max 2.

Other headphones – Worthy AirPods alternatives

Beats

If AirPods aren’t in your budget, Apple also sells a line of Beats headphones and earbuds that offer many of the same features for a lower price, including the popular on-ear Solo 4 and Powerbeats Pro 2. We’ll also track headphone deals in our roundup of the best earbuds for iPhone and best over-ear headphones if you’d like to see deals on other brands.

U.S. Black Friday price: There is $150 off the Beats Studio Pro and $100 off the Solo 4 at Amazon, but we expect to see more discounts later in November.

U.K. Black Friday price: There is £90 off the Powerbeats Pro 2 and £100 off the Powerbeats Fit at Amazon, but we expect to see more discounts later in November.

Latest AirPods deals

The tables below compare current prices with each model’s lowest recorded price and full retail price.

U.S. deals

U.K. deals

Should you buy AirPods now?

David Price / Foundry

Black Friday is here, and we’d buy now if the AirPods you want are at or near their lowest price. Some of last year’s best deals sold out, so if you see a price you’re happy with, it’s worth buying while the offer is still available.

At $149, AirPods Pro 3 are $20 cheaper than the previous lowest price we tracked. For AirPods Max 2, use the $399 price we saw during June Prime Day as a benchmark. If today’s price is well above that, we’d wait for a bigger discount.

AirPods 5 saw little in the way of discounts during October Prime Day. If you find a substantial Black Friday saving, we’d buy now. If they’re still close to full price and you’re in no hurry, we’d wait.

Compare prices before you order. Check Walmart and Best Buy as well as Amazon in the U.S. In the U.K., Argos had competitive deals last Black Friday. For more advice, see our guide to the best time to buy AirPods.

Should you buy an old pair of AirPods?

Older-generation AirPods can be a good buy at the right clearance price. Compare their actual selling price with the discounted price of their replacement, rather than focusing on the percentage saving from an old launch price. A substantial discount can make an older pair worthwhile; a small difference may leave you sacrificing useful features for little saving.

AirPods 4 are harder to recommend now that AirPods 5 include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, starting at the same $129 price previously charged for AirPods 4 without ANC. Check which AirPods 4 version you’re buying—there were models with and without noise cancellation—and look for a substantial saving over AirPods 5.

AirPods Pro 2 remain worth considering if they’re significantly cheaper than Pro 3. However, the newer model improves fit, noise cancellation, and battery life, while adding heart-rate sensing. Compare their sale prices carefully: a strong Pro 3 discount could make the older pair’s clearance offer less attractive.

The original AirPods Max also need a substantial discount to justify choosing them over Max 2. The newer headphones add the H2 chip, improved noise cancellation, and features including Adaptive Audio and Conversation Awareness. Check the generation rather than relying on the charging port alone: the original AirPods Max were also sold in a USB-C version.

Buying older stock new is different from buying used or refurbished AirPods. For those pairs, check the stated condition, charging case, warranty, and returns policy, and buy from a reputable seller. Be cautious about battery condition and unusually low marketplace prices, since convincing counterfeits can resemble genuine AirPods. Our guide explains how to spot fake AirPods.

For more advice, see our AirPods buying guide and guide to the best time to buy AirPods.

AirPods deals to avoid

Foundry

Check exactly what an offer includes before comparing prices. Different charging-case packages can affect features and value, so make sure you’re comparing equivalent versions. Also check any spending requirements, contracts, or rebates attached to offers advertising “free” AirPods.

Judge the price against previous selling prices as well as the advertised discount. A large saving from the recommended retail price doesn’t necessarily mean a particularly good deal if retailers regularly charge less.

Check whether the listing is for a new, refurbished, or used pair. For used or refurbished AirPods, look for clear information about condition, warranty, and returns coverage. Battery condition deserves particular caution: a low purchase price may be less attractive if listening time has deteriorated.

Finally, check who is selling and dispatching your order, particularly when shopping through a marketplace. Unusually low prices from unfamiliar sellers warrant caution, since counterfeit AirPods can look convincing. Our guide explains how to tell if AirPods are fake.

How we choose AirPods deals

Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on AirPods reviews. We consider sound quality, noise cancellation, comfort, battery life, and everyday use – not just the specifications or advertised saving.

Our testing helps us explain which features are worth paying for. For example, our AirPods Pro 3 review assessed how securely the redesigned ear tips stayed in place during exercise, checked battery life against Apple’s claims, and evaluated the heart-rate sensor. Our AirPods Max 2 review weighed their excellent sound and noise cancellation against drawbacks including weight and the Smart Case.

We combine those findings with current prices and previous lows to judge whether an offer represents good value. Our Best AirPods guide explains why the most expensive model isn’t necessarily the best choice for everyone: fit, listening habits, and the features you need all matter.

PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 28, 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout the Black Friday weekend

Black Friday is one of the best opportunities to save on a Mac, with retailers competing to discount MacBooks and desktop models – including recently released machines. The Black Friday Mac deals are already here, and the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with 512GB of storage is where we’d start for most people. Amazon has listed it for $999 in the U.S. and £1,149 in the U.K., saving $300 and about £150 off Apple’s current prices. If you already have a display, keyboard, and mouse, the M6 Mac mini is a cheaper way to get a new Mac at $779 or £692.

There are bigger savings on MacBook Pro models if you need the extra power. In the U.S., Amazon has listed the 14-inch M5 Max MacBook Pro with 36GB of memory and 2TB of storage for $3,599, $500 off. But, if you think you’d benefit from the OLED display, the 16-inch touchscreen MacBook Pro is $300 off. In the U.K., the 16-inch M5 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory and 1TB of storage is £2,599, £400 off.

Apple’s June price increases make the advertised savings worth a closer look. The U.S. MacBook Air deal is $50 below its pre-increase price, while the U.K. offer is still about £50 above what Apple charged before June. We compare prices for the same configurations so you can see which deals are worth taking and which have been better before.

Below, we explain which Mac to buy at these prices, from the budget MacBook Neo to the Mac Studio. If you’re deciding whether to buy from a reseller or from Apple, compare what you’d pay today with what you’d actually gain from a gift card on a future purchase. For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our Apple Black Friday deals roundups for the best iPad deals, Apple Watch deals and AirPods deals.

Apple Store Black Friday offer: From November 27 to 30, Apple is offering a gift card worth $200/£160 with either size of M5 MacBook Air, $250/£200 with an eligible 14-inch M5 Pro or M5 Max MacBook Pro, $300/£240 with an eligible 16-inch M5 Pro or M5 Max MacBook Pro, and $100/£80 with an eligible Mac mini. The gift card is for a future Apple purchase. Compare its value with the upfront discounts we share below. See the full Apple Black Friday offer.

Which Mac or MacBook should you buy this Black Friday?

MacBook Air – Our best overall choice

Ida Blix

The MacBook Air is our recommendation for most buyers. Both sizes offer a lightweight, silent laptop for everyday work, studying, and occasional creative projects. Choose the 13-inch for portability or the 15-inch for more workspace without MacBook Pro pricing.

We’d prioritize a competitive price on the memory and storage you need. For regular lengthy exports or other sustained demanding tasks, consider a MacBook Pro with active cooling instead.

U.S. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought the 13-inch M5 Air with 16GB memory and 512GB storage to $1,099, and the equivalent 15-inch to $1,299. We are seeing up to $400 off the 13-inch models, and $399 off the 1TB 15-inch MacBook Air, bringing the price below Apple’s pre-increase list price. These savings are better than Apple’s $200 gift card.

U.K. Black Friday price: October offers included approximately £1,199 for the 13-inch M5 Air and £1,349 for the 15-inch, both with 512GB storage. Last Black Friday’s M4 models with 256GB reached £849 and £1,025. Match storage capacities when comparing generations. Amazon has the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with 512GB of storage, 16GB of memory, and an 8-core GPU for £1,149, saving £150 off Apple’s £1,299 price. That’s about £50 less than it cost during October Prime Day. Amazon also has the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air with 512GB of storage and 16GB of memory for £1,299, saving £200 off Apple’s £1,499 price. Earlier in November, we saw a larger £200 discount on the 13-inch MacBook Air.

The £160 Apple gift card is close to the £150 upfront discount on the 13-inch 512GB Air.

Apple’s Deal: Apple’s £160 gift card is worth about £10 more than Amazon’s upfront discount on the 13-inch model. On the 15-inch model, Amazon’s upfront discount is £40 more than the gift card’s value.

MacBook Neo – Our budget choice, at the right price

Eugen Wegmann

The MacBook Neo suits browsing, schoolwork, streaming, and office apps. Its lower starting price makes it appealing, but its fixed 8GB of memory leaves less room for demanding workloads.

Check which configuration is discounted: only the 512GB version includes Touch ID. Both lack a backlit keyboard, MagSafe, and Thunderbolt. Compare clearance MacBook Air stock before deciding how much those compromises save you.

U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has the 256GB MacBook Neo for $599 ($100 off) and the 512GB model with Touch ID for $699 ($100 off) – the prices Apple charged before its June price increase for those models.

U.K. Black Friday price: The 256GB MacBook Neo is £609.97, £89 off, but the 512GB model with Touch ID is an even better deal at £697 (£102 off).

MacBook Pro M6 – Best step up from the Air

Halyna Kubiv

The standard M6 MacBook Pro is worth considering if you want a better built-in display, more connections, and cooling for sustained workloads without paying for a Pro or Max chip. It comes in a 14-inch size, with a non-touch Liquid Retina XDR display, HDMI, and an SDXC card slot.

It starts with 16GB memory and 1TB storage, so account for those specifications when comparing prices with an Air or older Pro. Despite the newer generation number, the standard M6 isn’t automatically the better choice for demanding work than an M5 Pro or M5 Max.

U.S. Black Friday price: The M6 model wasn’t available during October Prime Day, but it’s on offer for Black Friday with $250 off at Amazon, where it’s $1,749. B&H also has $150 off the 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6)

U.K. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the older 14-inch M5 with 16GB memory and 1TB storage reached approximately £1,619. Amazon has the 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro with 16GB of memory and 1TB of storage for £1,829.97, saving £169.03. That’s just £30.97 more than the equivalent M5 model at £1,799, so we’d buy the M6.

MacBook Pro M5 Pro – Best for demanding professional work

Foundry

The non-touchscreen M5 Pro MacBook Pro is a strong choice for development, photography, video editing, and heavier multitasking. Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, it offers professional performance without the Max chip’s higher price.

Compare it with the touchscreen version using the same memory and storage. Both offer M5 Pro configurations, so a discounted non-touch model could be particularly good value if its existing XDR display meets your needs.

U.S. Black Friday price: October prices included $2,339 for the 14-inch M5 Pro with 24GB memory and 1TB storage, and $2,749 for the equivalent 16-inch. So far this Black Friday we are seeing $300 off the 16-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and $300 off the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro. Note that Amazon takes $250 off upfront while Apple offers $250 or $300 (depending on the model) in future credit, so it might be worth taking advantage of Apple’s deal if you are likely to want to make future Apple purchases.

U.K. Black Friday price: The equivalent configurations reached approximately £2,250 and £2,700. Last Black Friday, selected previous-generation M4 Pro models received discounts of around £350. The 14-inch MacBook Pro is £2,289 (£210 off at Amazon), while Amazon’s deal on the 16-inch M5 Pro MacBook Pro is £2,599, is £400 off, beating Apple’s £240 Gift card offer in the U.K.

Apple’s Deal: Apple will give a $250 U.S. or £200 U.K. Apple Gift Card with a 14-inch MacBook Pro M5 Pro or M5 Max and a $300 U.S. or £240 U.K. Apple Gift Card with a 16-inch MacBook Pro M5 Pro or M5 Max.

MacBook Pro M5 Max – Best for demanding graphics and video

Ida Blix

Consider the non-touchscreen M5 Max MacBook Pro if your work benefits from additional graphics power or more memory than an M5 Pro supports. Complex 3D projects and demanding video production make a stronger case for it than everyday productivity.

We’d choose the configuration around the work you do. A larger advertised discount on a Max doesn’t necessarily make it better value than a less expensive Pro that meets your needs. Our MacBook Pro buying advice explains the options.

U.S. Black Friday price: October offers included $3,499 for a 14-inch M5 Max with 2TB storage and $3,899 for a 16-inch with 36GB memory and 2TB storage. Last Black Friday, selected M4 Max configurations were $500 off and this Black Friday month we are already seeing $500 off the M5 Max models.

U.K. Black Friday price: In the U.K., both the 14-inch MacBook Pro and 16-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Max are currently on offer for £3,999 each.

Touchscreen MacBook Pro – Best for its OLED display

Roman Loyola/Foundry

The touchscreen MacBook Pro is most compelling for its OLED display and thinner, lighter design. Improved blacks and reduced blooming could matter more to your everyday experience than touch controls, particularly if you spend most of your working day using the built-in screen.

Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, these models offer comparable processing performance to their non-touch equivalents. Compare matching configurations: the regular premium is $400/£400, so consider how much you’ll benefit from the display before paying extra.

U.S. Black Friday price: These models arrived in November, so there are no equivalent October Prime Day or Black Friday 2025 prices. So far, we’re seeing $300 off the 16-inch touchscreen MacBook Pro.

U.K. Black Friday price: In the U.K. we have seen Amazon knock £244 off the price of the MacBook Pro PROLED XDR Display (14-inch, M5 Pro, 1TB, Touchscreen), although it’s now £244 off.

Mac mini M6 – Our best-value desktop choice

Foundry

The M6 Mac mini suits buyers who already own a display, keyboard, and mouse. It offers a compact desktop for everyday work and lighter creative projects. Check storage carefully: the entry-level model has a restrictive 256GB SSD.

U.S. Black Friday price: October’s entry-level M6 mini reached approximately $780. Last Black Friday, the older M4 equivalent was $479. So far this November we’ve seen $150 off the 512GB model.

U.K. Black Friday price: October’s M6 model reached approximately £824, compared with £499 for the M4 last Black Friday. For Black Friday the deal is even better at £207 off the 256GB Mac mini – the best price we’ve seen at £692.

Apple’s Deal: Apple will give a $100 U.S. or £80 U.K. Apple Gift Card with a Mac mini purchase.

Mac mini M5 Pro – Best compact desktop for professional work

Ida Blix

The M5 Pro mini offers more processing power and memory capacity for demanding work without moving to a Studio. Compare upgraded configurations carefully: if the total approaches Mac Studio pricing, check which machine better suits your workload.

U.S. Black Friday price: The 24GB/512GB M5 Pro mini reached approximately $1,550 in October. Last Black Friday’s M4 Pro equivalent was $1,249. So far this November we’ve seen $150 off the 512GB model.

U.K. Black Friday price: October’s M5 Pro configuration reached approximately £1,647. The previous-generation M4 Pro with 24GB/512GB was £1,269 last Black Friday. There is £244 off the 512GB Mac mini M5 Pro in the U.K.

Apple’s Deal: Apple will give a $100 U.S. or £80 U.K. Apple Gift Card with a Mac mini purchase.

iMac – Best complete desktop setup

Foundry

The iMac combines a 24-inch 4.5K display with the computer and matching accessories. Compare the two-port and four-port versions carefully: the latter adds processing power, connections, and a Touch ID keyboard. Factor those differences into the final price.

U.S. Black Friday price: The M6 wasn’t available during October Prime Day. The entry-level M4 predecessor reached approximately $1,360 in October and $1,149 last Black Friday (before the $200 June price increase). We are seeing $100 off the iMac M6 at Amazon with a coupon on the listing page, bringing the price down to $1,399 for the first time.

U.K. Black Friday price: October’s four-port M4 with 256GB storage was £1,620. Last Black Friday, comparable four-port M4 stock reached £1,349. These are predecessor prices rather than M6 targets. There’s £100 off the M4 iMac.

Mac Studio – Best for demanding desktop workflows

Stephan Wiesend

The M5 Max Studio suits demanding graphics, video, and other professional workloads. Compare it with the M5 Pro mini first. The considerably more expensive M5 Ultra is for exceptional workloads requiring its additional performance and memory; most buyers won’t need it. Budget for a display and peripherals.

U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has the M5 Max Mac Studio with 36GB of memory and 512GB of storage for $2,299, matching October Prime Day’s $200 discount.

U.K. Black Friday price: The Mac Studio was £209 off in the U.K., but it’s back to full price now.

Latest Mac & MacBook Deals

Check below to find the best price we are seeing right now for each configuration compared to the best price we have ever seen and the full price.

U.S. deals

U.K. deals

Should you buy a Mac or MacBook now?

Black Friday is here, and we’d buy now if the Mac you want is at or near the lowest price we’ve seen for that configuration. If you’re shopping for a clearance model in a specific screen size, memory configuration, or finish, it’s worth taking a good deal while it’s in stock.

If a retailer’s discount is close to the value of Apple’s gift card and you already have another Apple purchase planned, buying from Apple could be worthwhile. Check eligibility first. The MacBook Neo, standard M6 MacBook Pro, iMac, and Mac Studio are excluded from Apple’s Black Friday gift card offer.

The M5 MacBook Air is a good buy at a substantial discount, with a replacement unlikely before 2027. The recently updated Mac mini and Mac Studio are also worth buying if the configuration you need is on sale.

The standard M6 MacBook Pro and OLED touchscreen models are now available, though discounts may be modest so soon after launch. A discounted M5 Pro or M5 Max MacBook Pro could be better value if you can do without the touchscreen model’s improved display and lighter design. If your M4 or M5 MacBook Pro still meets your needs, we’d hold on to it. See our MacBook Pro buying advice.

The M6 iMac has just replaced the M4 model. If the price gap is small, we’d go for the M6. A steep clearance discount could make the M4 the better buy.

Check price history before you order. Apple raised prices in June, so a Mac on sale today could still cost more than it did at full price before the increase. Compare Amazon with Best Buy, Walmart, and B&H in the U.S. and with Currys and John Lewis in the U.K.

Which Mac specifications are worth paying for?

The cheapest Mac isn’t always the best value. Use Black Friday to get a configuration that will serve you for longer within your budget, but don’t pay for performance or features you won’t use.

Check the exact chip, screen size, memory, and storage. A standard M6 and an M5 Pro or M5 Max serve different needs: the newer generation number alone doesn’t tell you which is better for your work. For MacBook Pro listings, distinguish the OLED touchscreen version from non-touch models.

Avoid saving a small amount by buying too little memory or storage. Most current Macs start with 16GB of unified memory, but the MacBook Neo has a fixed 8GB, and some desktop configurations include only a 256GB SSD. Unified memory cannot be upgraded later. An external SSD can add storage, but it cannot compensate for insufficient RAM.

Once the processor meets your needs, additional memory may be more useful than a faster chip. Compare a discounted Air with the Neo, too: the M5 Air starts with twice the memory and storage of the entry-level Neo. Our Mac buying guide explains which specifications suit different workloads.

Check whether the configuration includes nano-texture glass. This optional finish reduces glare and reflections, which can help in bright rooms or near windows, but increases the price. If reflections rarely bother you, standard glass may offer better value.

Should you buy an older Mac or MacBook?

Foundry

An older Mac can be excellent value if its price reflects its age and configuration. Compare its actual selling price with the discounted price of the newer equivalent, rather than focusing on a large percentage saving from its original launch price.

Previous-generation Apple silicon models are the most promising starting point. A discounted M4 MacBook Air or standard M5 MacBook Pro may meet your needs comfortably. Older Pro and Max configurations can also be worth considering if they provide the memory, graphics performance, and connections your work requires for substantially less money.

Check what the saving buys—and what you give up. An older Mac with more memory or storage could be more useful than a newer entry-level configuration. Conversely, a cheaper older Air with 256GB storage isn’t directly comparable with an M5 Air that starts with 512GB. The non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pros also remain current options, despite the arrival of the standard M6 and touchscreen models.

Be much more cautious with Intel Macs. Their software support is winding down, and a low purchase price may leave you with a machine that has a limited useful life for current apps and macOS features. Check compatibility with the software you need before buying any older model.

For used or refurbished Macs, check battery condition on laptops, warranty coverage, and the returns policy. Confirm that Activation Lock has been removed and that the Mac isn’t still enrolled in an organization’s management system.

For more advice read:

  • Should I buy a MacBook Neo?
  • Should I buy a MacBook Air?
  • Should I buy a MacBook Pro?
  • Should I buy a Mac mini?
  • Should I buy a Mac Studio?

Mac or MacBook deals to avoid

Treat large advertised discounts carefully. Following June’s price increases, “$400 off” may simply bring a Mac closer to what it cost before the increase. Compare previous selling prices for the same configuration, rather than judging the offer solely against today’s recommended price.

Check whether the price includes AppleCare+ or another protection plan. Some Amazon listings bundle coverage with the Mac. If you don’t want it, a listing without coverage could be cheaper; if you do, compare the bundle with buying the Mac and coverage separately.

Check for a bundled power adapter, too. Some Mac laptops are sold without one in the U.K. and EU. A charger bundle may be useful if you need an adapter, but could mean paying extra unnecessarily if you already own a suitable one.

Compare the complete setup cost. A Mac mini or Studio requires a display, keyboard, and mouse or trackpad, while adapters and docks can add to the cost of any Mac.

Finally, distinguish cash discounts from gift cards, trade-ins, financing, and membership-only offers. Read the conditions, check the seller, and confirm whether the Mac is new, refurbished, or used, along with its warranty and returns policy.

How we choose Mac and MacBook deals

Macworld has covered the Mac since its launch in 1984, and our recommendations draw on decades of experience and hands-on reviews. We consider performance, display quality, battery life, portability, connectivity, and everyday use alongside price to explain which Macs suit different buyers.

Our reviews help us assess which upgrades are worth paying for. We look at whether additional processing power benefits demanding workloads, when more memory is useful, and whether a premium display justifies the extra cost. A MacBook Air may offer better value for everyday work, while a Pro, Max, or Ultra configuration needs to earn its higher price through the work it enables.

We combine those findings with current prices and previous offers, matching the exact chip, screen size, memory, and storage. Following Apple’s June price increases, we also consider earlier selling prices rather than judging a deal solely against today’s recommended retail price. A large advertised discount doesn’t automatically make an offer exceptional.

We consider the complete purchase, too: the retailer, product condition, warranty, and any conditions attached to the price. For desktop Macs, we also account for the display and accessories you’ll need. Our Mac buying guide and MacBook comparison explain how to choose the right model and configuration.

FAQ
